entries.name: bcc - Bruce's C Compiler
entries.description: Bruce's C compiler is a simple C compiler that produces 8086 assembler for tiny/small memory models.

entries.name: DJGPP
entries.description: DJ Delorie's complete 32-bit C/C++ development environment for Intel 80386. Used for Quake.

entries.name: GCC IA-16 toolchain
entries.description: A 16-bit counterpart to DJGPP, a GCC-based toolchain for developing 16-bit (8086 to 80286, a.k.a. IA-16) DOS applications, currently maintained by TK Chia.

entries.name: Insight
entries.description: Very small debugger for real-mode DOS programs with Borland's Turbo like UI. Features an i80486 disassembler, and i8086 assembler.

entries.name: documentation
entries.description: is very valuable in order to understand working with both version 1.9 and the V2 fork.

entries.name: Open Watcom
entries.description: Formerly commercial C/C++ development environment for 16- and 32-bit DOS and Windows. The current official version is 1.9. A GitHub fork is also available. Used for Doom I-II, Warcraft I-II, Duke Nukem 3D, Full Throttle, Dark Forces and Retro City Rampage.

entries.name: Open Watcom V2
entries.description: GitHub fork which is actively maintained and is ported to 64-bit Windows and Linux.

entries.name: Turbo C 2.01
entries.description: C IDE and compiler from Borland first released in 1987.

entries.name: Turbo C++ 1.01
entries.description: C++ IDE and compiler from Borland released in 1991.

entries.name: Turbo C++ 3.0
entries.description: C++ IDE and compiler from Borland released in 1992.

entries.name: DIV Games Studio 2
entries.description: IDE to develop DOS games in 2d, mode 7 and 3d. Released in 1998.

entries.name: T3X
entries.description: A small, portable, procedural, block-structured, recursive, almost typeless, and to some degree object-oriented programming language by Nils M. Holm.

entries.name: SmallerC
entries.description: Portable self-hosting C compiler capable of producing executables for a number of platforms, including real and protected mode DOS programs, by Alexei A. Frounze.

entries.name: Small-C Toolkit
entries.description: A self-hosting Small-C Compiler Toolkit for DOS(8086) with: K&R C Compiler, Make, Linker, Assembler. First released in 1982 by Jim E. Hendrix.

entries.name: 386MAX
entries.description: Memory manager for DOS PCs with 386 or higher CPUs, released by Qualitas company in 1992. Source code was released in June 2022 on GitHub with GPL-3.0 license.

entries.name: DOjS
entries.description: JavaScript programming environment for MS-DOS, FreeDOS or any DOS-based Windows (like 95, 98, ME).

entries.name: Lua for DOS
entries.description: Online demo of Lua 5.3.5, compiled for MS-DOS on the Intel 80486 processor.
section: Scripting languages and interpreters for DOS

entries.name: Micropython for FreeDOS
entries.description: FreeDOS ad-hoc module for micropython.
section: Scripting languages and interpreters for DOS

entries.name: perldos
entries.description: Perl for DOS.
section: Scripting languages and interpreters for DOS

entries.name: PythonD
entries.description: Python for DOS, including multi-threading, networking and OpenGL.
section: Scripting languages and interpreters for DOS

entries.name: The Life of MS-DOS by Brendan Byers
entries.description: History of the DOS family including CP/M, Q-DOS/86-DOS, MS-DOS and PC-DOS. Article also includes a diagram of the timeline and family tree of DOS operating systems.

entries.name: 80x86 16-bit Compiling How-to by Alexei A. Frounze
entries.description: 16-bit compilation tutorial for Borland/Turbo C/C++ and Open Watcom. Goes into depth of memory addressing and memory models.

entries.name: 32bit DOS development with Open Watcom
entries.description: 32-bit compilation tutorial for Open Watcom.

entries.name: How to build DOS COM files with GCC by Chris Wellons
entries.description: Build process of Chris Wellons's DOS Defender game using DJGPP. Goal was to create a 32-bit 80386 COM executable.

entries.name: David Brackeen - 256-Color VGA Programming in C
entries.description: Tutorial series to learn how to create graphics on DOS, written in 1996.

entries.name: 640k Really is Enough for Anyone by Robert W. Oliver II
entries.description: Short article about getting Turbo C running on FreeDOS and moving a pixel around.

entries.name: Just keeping it real... old skool style - Scali's OpenBlog
entries.description: Blog post about Scali's journey of doing CGA, EGA and VGA programming.

entries.name: Alex Russell's Dos Game Programming in C for Beginners
entries.description: DOS game programming tutorial series including a primer on C, graphics, animation, input handling and collision detection. This series contains a tutorial for making buffered input handling. Last chapter contains full source code of a Break Out game on DOS.

entries.name: The Artevida Game Programming Tutorials
entries.description: Kevin Matz's almost book-length treatment of DOS system programming and VGA programming fundamentals using C/C++ and 80x86 assembly. Unfortunately it is incomplete and was abandoned since 2001.

entries.name: PC Game Programmer's Encyclopedia
entries.description: Collection of guides covering assembly, sound (Sound Blaster, Gravis UltraSound, PC Speaker, GameBlaster, Adlib), input, memory (EMS, XMS, DMA Transfers), PIT, VGA, SVGA, algorithms and file formats.

entries.name: The Art of Demomaking by flipcode
entries.description: Series from 1999 that introduces to graphics programming under DOS. The home site contains other late 90s/early 2000s game programming articles as well.

entries.name: Programming MS-DOS with Power - DOS Programming, Undocumented DOS, and DOS Secrets
entries.description: System programming tutorials like disk handling, interrupts, inputs, sound, graphics.

entries.name: Programmer's Heaven (InfoMagic)(March 1997) CD-ROM
entries.description: Source code and files for the following topics: MS-DOS, networking, C, C++, Pascal, Visual Basic, Delphi, 3D, PC speaker, Soundblaster, Gravis Ultrasound, MIDI and many more.

entries.name: bios.h header documentation by Digital Mars
entries.description: API documentation for routines accessing BIOS operations directly (disk operations, BIOS keyboard, printer, time, memory, serial, interrupts).

entries.name: Part 1
entries.description: Part 2 - API documentation of functions for interfacing with the DOS operating system itself.

entries.name: Ralph Brown's Interrupt List - HTML version
entries.description: List of every documented and undocumented interrupt call known, accessible through search, categories and interrupt numbers.

entries.name: A look back at memory models in 16-bit MS-DOS
entries.description: Raymond Chen's explanation of segmented memory, including near- and far pointers.

entries.name: Values for standard video mode
entries.description: List of all known video modes including BIOS interrupt numbers, text/pixel resolution, number of colors and video memory addresses.

entries.name: Color Graphics Adapter: Notes
entries.description: Document describing the hardware, memory map, register I/O and hardware clones of the IBM's original CGA.

entries.name: VGA Hardware - OSDev wiki
entries.description: Hardware guide for VGA cards that is also relevant for modern graphics cards including NVidia and ATI.

entries.name: Graphical programming in Assembly (DOS)
entries.description: A VGA programming tutorial that also shows the list of video modes (text, CGA, EGA, VGA, SVGA) in a table at the beginning.

entries.name: VGA programming lessons
entries.description: VGA programming tutorial series in Pascal and Assembly.

entries.name: DOS Super VGA / VESA programming notes - by Myles
entries.description: VESA article with history at the beginning and short mention of the VESA VBE standard, but unfortunately the example codes aren't even available through Wayback Machine.

entries.name: VESA Video Modes - OSDev wiki
entries.description: Tutorial about querying VESA modes.

entries.name: DJGPP VESA guide
entries.description: Tutorial about querying VESA modes.

entries.name: High-res high-speed VESA tutorial
entries.description: Series of tutorials that include drawing pixels in VESA mode (protected or real).

entries.name: C code sample for drawing in VESA 2.0 mode
entries.description: Just code listing for drawing an ellipse in VESA mode.

entries.name: Programming Sound Cards CD
entries.description: A 1995 CD-ROM containing source code for Adlib, Gravis, Pro-Audio, Roland and Sound Blaster sound cards. The description for the folders on the CD-ROM is listed on the back of the CD-ROM case.

entries.name: Making some noise with the PC speaker! - by Mark Feldman
entries.description: Very short tutorial on using the PIT for generating PC speaker frequency.

entries.name: Frequencies of Musical Notes
entries.description: Freqency table usable to parameterize the PC speaker.

entries.name: Sound Programming with PC Speaker - Chapter 23 of A to Z of C
entries.description: PC speaker programming chapter of the "A to Z of C" book with source code.

entries.name: Yamaha YM3812 (OPL2) sound chip Wikipedia article
entries.description: Best starting point to learn about the OPL2 sound chip besides 8-bit guy's YouTube video.

entries.name: The Ad Lib Music Synthesizer Card Programming Guide - by Tero Töttö
entries.description: Reference of OPL2 operations and registers.

entries.name: Programmer's Guide to the Yamaha YMF 262/OPL3 FM Music Synthesizer
entries.description: Reverse-engineered reference on OPL3.

entries.name: Sound Blaster 16 Programming Document 3.5 by Ethan Brodsky
entries.description: Programming the Sound Blaster 16 DSP CT1341 chip for recording and playback of digitized audio.

entries.name: Soundblaster Programming Information v0.90
entries.description: List of Sound Blaster models and registers.

entries.name: Table of DOSBox cyclecounts according to processor types
entries.description: A table for setting the appropriate DOSBox cycle count according to CPU types (IBM XT 88, 286, 386, 486, Pentium I, Pentium II). Comes handy when you are developing a DOS game and want to simulate the environment where you intend to execute it.

entries.name: Game Engine Black Book: Wolfenstein 3D - by Fabien Sanglard
entries.description: Fabien Sanglard's walkthrough on the game engine architecture of id Software's Wolfenstein 3D on the IBM PC's hardware. Contains forewords by John Carcmack, Tom Hall and John Romero.

entries.name: Game Engine Black Book: Doom - by Fabien Sanglard
entries.description: Fabien Sanglard's walkthrough on the game engine architecture of id Software's original Doom on Intel 486 system and game console ports. Contains forewords by John Carcmack, Dave Taylor and John Romero.

entries.name: A to Z of C - a book on C/DOS programming by K. Joseph Wesley and R. Rajesh Jeba Anbiah
entries.description: Non-profit book on programming in C on DOS. DOS system programming starts from Part II.

entries.name: Michael Abrash's Graphics Programming Black Book Special Edition
entries.description: Collection of Michael Abrash's Dr. Dobb's Journal graphics programming articles and his work on the graphics subsystem of Quake (mirror).

entries.name: Open Library link
entries.description: , Internet Archive link

entries.name: Tricks of the Game-Programming Gurus - by Andre Lamothe, John Ratcliff and Denise Tyler
entries.description: Comprehensive DOS game development book about starting out. Topics include keyboard, mouse- and joystick input handling, creating 2D and 3D VGA graphics, raycaster rendering, sound and music, game algorithms, Interrupt Service Routines (ISR), timers, artificial intelligence, networked multiplayer through serial port and null-modem cable, tooling, parallax scrolling and optimization techniques.

entries.name: Open Library link
entries.description: , Internet Archive link

entries.name: More Tricks of the Game Programming Gurus - by Greg Anderson
entries.description: Companion book to Tricks of the Game Programming Gurus, continuing where the original left off. Topics include SVGA, Binary Space Partition (BSP), UI, voxel graphics, memory management in real and protected mode, advanced sound programming, debugging and optimization techniques.

entries.name: Why DOS Was (and Is) a Thing - FreeDOS
entries.description: Historical talk starting from Unix, going through CPM, DOS 1.x, DOS 2.x, DOS 3.x, DOS 4.x, DOS 6.x, Windows 3.1, Windows 95 and ending with FreeDOS.

entries.name: CGA Graphics - Not as bad as you thought! - by 8-bit Guy
entries.description: History and technical details about IBM's CGA system. Also describes 4-color RGBI and 16-color Composite modes.

entries.name: How Oldschool Sound/Music worked - by 8-bit Guy
entries.description: Video about PC speaker, FM synthesizers in NES and Commodore 64, Yamaha OPL chip in AdLib and Sound Blaster sound cards, PCM samples and MOD music.

entries.name: Let's Code - MS DOS - by root42
entries.description: DOS programming tutorial series including VGA, SoundBlaster and VGA Mode X.

entries.name: LGR - Evolution of PC Audio - As Told by Secret of Monkey Island
entries.description: Comparison of playing the intro theme of Secret of Monkey Island through PC speaker, IBM PCjr/Tandy, AdLib, Game Blaster, Roland LAPC-1/MT-32, Gravis Ultrasound, Roland SCC-1 MIDI, SB16 Waveblaster/AWE32 and CD quality digital audio.

entries.name: Porting Retro City Rampage to MS-DOS: From PS4 to 1.44MB Floppy
entries.description: GDC talk. Brian Provinciano's presentation on porting Retro City Rampage from PlayStation 4 to DOS. Topics include optimization, using interrupts, timing, PC speaker sound, joystick, memory management and fixed-point math.

entries.name: DOS Executables Explained - Nostalgia Nerd
entries.description: Video about DOS executable formats including .COM, .BAT and .EXE.

entries.name: Why does DOS use 8.3 Filenames? - Nostalgia Nerd
entries.description: Video about the 8.3 limitation of filenames under DOS, FAT partitioning scheme, NTFS, VFAT, FatGo, and LFN.EXE.

entries.name: What is DOS Protected Mode? / DOS Extenders- Nostalgia Nerd
entries.description: Video about how PC memory looks like, conventional memory, extender memory and reasons for the need of DOS Protected Mode Interface (DPMI) and extenders like DOS/4GW.

entries.name: MS-DOS has been Open-Sourced! We Build and Run it! - Dave's Garage
entries.description: Former Microsoft employee David Plummer tells stories about development of MS-DOS and compiles MS-DOS 4.00 source code which has been open-sourced by Microsoft.

entries.name: MS-DOS
entries.description: GitHub repository of the original source code for MS-DOS v1.25, v2.0 and v4.0, open-sourced by Microsoft.

entries.name: FreeDOS
entries.description: FreeDOS is an open source DOS-compatible operating system that you can use to play classic DOS games, run legacy business software, or develop embedded systems. Any program that works on MS-DOS should also run on FreeDOS.

entries.name: Allegro 4.2
entries.description: Game development library for DOS, Windows and Linux. 4.2 version supports DOS platform.

entries.name: LoveDOS
entries.description: A framework for making 2D DOS games in Lua. API based on a subset of the LÖVE API.

entries.name: DOS-VGA-Game
entries.description: Marco A. Marrero's DOS VGA/hardware library implemented in assembly and Turbo Pascal.

entries.name: DIGPAK sound drivers source code
entries.description: Original source code for the DIGPAK sound drivers uploaded to GitHub by John W. Ratcliff.

entries.name: DOS Defender
entries.description: Christopher Wellons's x86 real mode DOS Asteroids clone created as an entry for Lundum Dare #31.

entries.name: Dungeons of Noudar
entries.description: First-person 2.5D dungeon-crawler on protected mode. Written in C++, includes software rendering, fixed point math, test coverage and sound (PC speaker, Adlib, OPL2LPT).

entries.name: Emeritus Pong
entries.description: Pong clone for DOS, Windows and Linux. Uses PC speaker for sound on DOS.

entries.name: Floppy Bird
entries.description: Flappy Bird clone written in 16 bit assembly. Not a DOS program, but a PC-Booter application instead (although it's also possible to build a COM executable for DOS).

entries.name: George M. Tzoumas's collection of MS-DOS games and utilities
entries.description: Turbo Pascal with few games in C and C++. Games include Nibbles, Connect Four, Ms Pacman clone and two arcade/platform games. One of them (ra2) was written using Allegro. Utilities are all written in Turbo Pascal, these include game system routines, file and disk utilities and terminate-and-stay-resident programs (TSR).

entries.name: Gold Mine Run!
entries.description: Platformer written in C using DJGPP.

entries.name: Gridfighter 3D
entries.description: '80s style arcade shooter written in Quickbasic. Also the very first known DOS game that supports Oculus Rift VR headset.

entries.name: Hangman
entries.description: Hangman clone written in Basic. Runs on at least 80286 processors and uses EGA graphics.

entries.name: Magenta's Maze
entries.description: 3D maze game using CGA graphics with algebra as theme.

entries.name: Mario
entries.description: Super Mario Bros clone written in Turbo Pascal.

entries.name: NetHack
entries.description: Descendant of the original NetHack rougelike game first released in 1987 available on multiple platforms.

entries.name: Piskworks
entries.description: Gomoku clone written in C. Works on DOS, ZX Spectrum, ZX81, ZX80, APPLE1, AS400 and Windows.

entries.name: Plutonium Caverns
entries.description: Overhead puzzle game written in C. Web version uses DOSBox ported to Emscripten to embed DOSBox into HTML5. However, the original executable is also downloadable and buildable with Open Watcom.

entries.name: Ptakovina
entries.description: Tetris clone written in C. Runs on DOS, Unix/Linux, ZX Spectrum and Windows.

entries.name: sudoku86
entries.description: Sudoku clone written in C. Runs on 8086/8088 CPU, uses CGA, MCGA or VGA graphics and uses a mouse.

entries.name: Tetris
entries.description: Tetris clone written in assembly.

entries.name: Towers of Hanoi
entries.description: Tower of Hanoi puzzle game written in Turbo Pascal. Originally released in 1996.

entries.name: x86 pong
entries.description: Text-mode Pong clone written in C. Runs as PC-Booter game and under DOS.

entries.name: zmiy
entries.description: Text-mode Snake clone written in C. Runs on 8086 DOS.

entries.name: C-Dogs
entries.description: Sequel to the original Cyberdogs. Ronny Wester, the original creator no longer maintains the website for the original C-Dogs, but multiple ports exists, including cdogs-sdl.

entries.name: Doom
entries.description: Sci-fi FPS developed by id Software where you fight demons from hell on Mars. The DOS-specific code for Doom could not be published because of a dependency to the licensed DMX sound library, hence why it's cleaned up and only the Linux source is there. However, the Heretic and Hexen projects contain the original DOS code in a way where DMX-related code is removed.

entries.name: SBEMU
entries.description: A TSR that emulates Sound Blaster and OPL3 in pure DOS using modern PCI-based (onboard and add-in card) sound cards. Supports both real mode and protected mode games!

entries.description: A fork of SBEMU (see above), which also aims to offer Sound Blaster emulation for modern PC hardware, in both real mode and protected mode games.
